But the All Progressives Congress (APC) has dismissed the allegations as unfounded.
The SDP, in a statement by the spokesperson, Director of Contacts and Mobilisation, Hon. Jonathan Vatsa, to the SDP gubernatorial candidate in the state, Mohammed Ndarani Mohammed (SAN), in Minna on Tuesday, said funds in the state are being channelled to the governor’s campaign, leaving ongoing projects abandoned.
In addition to these, the SDP gubernatorial spokesperson claimed that over N10 billion has been expended on welfare and largess to different political groups who besieged Government House on a daily basis for solidarity visits.
Vatsa pointed out that while public funds are being wasted on campaign and political mobilisation by the governor ahead of the 2027 general elections, all ongoing projects across the state have been abandoned.
The former Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism in the state said that “any leader that has no respect for public funds, the implications are that the people suffer. That is exactly what is happening in the state under this administration.”
“This is one administration that spends public funds with recklessness, yet the people expect development; it doesn’t work,” Vatsa submitted.
He alleged that the recent presentation of seven expensive cars and ₦700 million cash to Hausa musicians, popularly referred to as Dauda Rarara, by the Governor is one of his many reckless spending of public funds.
He further alleged that the ruling All Progressives Congress has equally mapped out strategies to use insecurity-hit local government areas in the state to rig the forthcoming general elections, adding that “that is why the government has refused to address the security challenges in the state.”
“We have it in good authority that local government areas like Agwara, Mashegu, Shiroro, Rafi, Munya, Mariga and part of Paikoro, where there are serious security challenges, are the places they want to use to rig elections,” Vatsa alleged further.
Reacting to the allegations, the Director General Media to the Governor and Deputy Director Media to the campaign council, Alhaji Yahaya Idris, said the allegations were not true.
He said the money expended was far from what was alleged, saying, “Why quote this bogus figure all in the name of politics? It is not what APC will spend that kind of money; it is far, far less.”
On the N700 million allegedly given to Hausa film makers and singers, he said that also was unfounded, because the governor only promised to build a film village in the state based on seed money already on ground.
He therefore urged members of the public to disregard such propaganda and outright falsehood and check their facts instead of believing opposition elements who could not withstand the popularity of APC in the state.
